about.title: Los Altos Hills Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Los Altos Hills is a small town of roughly 8,400 people spread across quiet hillside roads. In 2025, its public collision record showed 34 injury crashes, 51 people hurt, and one traffic death. On paper, one is just a count. For the family behind it, it is everything. Collisions in town cluster along I-280, Page Mill Road, the I-280 southbound lanes, and Purissima Road, and they tend to peak on Tuesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., when commuters are heading home. If someone you love died because another driver, a property owner, or a company acted carelessly, California law lets certain family members bring a wrongful death claim in civil court. That claim runs separately from any criminal case and on its own clock: generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death claims for Santa Clara County families. We work on contingency and will lay out your options when you reach out.

whyChoose.title: Why Los Altos Hills Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, with a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can tell you plainly where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is real, and sometimes short
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, but when a government entity is involved, such as a claim tied to a state highway or county road, the window is much shorter. Getting started early protects your right to act.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there is nothing to pay up front. You only pay if we recover for you.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law puts a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children first in line. If none exist, certain financially dependent relatives or heirs may have standing. Because these rules are strict, it helps to have an attorney review your family situation before assuming you can or cannot file.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash on I-280 near Los Altos Hills. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It can. I-280 is a state highway, and if part of your claim involves a public agency such as Caltrans or Santa Clara County, California requires a government claim to be filed within months, not years, before a lawsuit is even possible. The general two-year deadline still applies to private parties like another driver. We can sort out which clocks are running in your case.

items.question: What losses can a wrongful death claim cover, and does the criminal case matter?
items.answer: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, so it proceeds independently of any criminal charges, whether or not the district attorney prosecutes. We cannot promise a result, but we can explain what the law allows and how each category of loss is evaluated.
